title: Checks for usage of .drain(..) for the sole purpose of clearing a container.
summary: This creates an unnecessary iterator that is dropped immediately. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of .clone() on a Copy type.
summary: The only reason Copy types implement Clone is for generics, not for using the clone method on a concrete type. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .clone() on a ref-counted pointer, (Rc, Arc, rc::Weak, or sync::Weak), and suggests calling Clone via unified function syntax instead (e.g., Rc::clone(foo)).
summary: Calling .clone() on an Rc, Arc, or Weak can obscure the fact that only the pointer is being cloned, not the underlying data. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of cloned() on an Iterator or Option where copied() could be used instead.
summary: copied() is better because it guarantees that the type being cloned implements Copy. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for slice references with cloned references such as &[f.clone()].
summary: Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.
